records.place: Escherndorf on the Main, in the Maindreieck, Franken

wine.name: Escherndorfer Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from Am Lumpen 1655, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Escherndorf
wine.sites: Am Lumpen 1655, the heart of the Escherndorfer Lump: a steep slope of about sixty per cent facing south at some 200 to 270 metres, opening on the valley of the Main like an amphitheatre that shuts out the north wind, on upper shell limestone.
wine.making: By the house's own sheet the must settles naturally and ferments with its own wild yeasts, no cultured yeast added, and the wine rests on its fine lees until the end of the following July before it is bottled dry. By the house's own pages every one of its Grosse Gewächse ferments with its own yeasts.
wine.glass: Lemon peel, kumquat and ripe pear over a peppery, herbal note and a faint bitterness of almond skin, with a salty, stony finish; dry and firm, built on acidity rather than breadth.
wine.ageing: Open and precise on release, it gains honey, nut and dried herbs over five to ten years and keeps longer in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; no need to decant, though a young bottle opens in the glass; a white wine glass.

label.means: The village and the Grosse Lage, named for the year the field name was first recorded.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.
Dry by the legal measure, as every Grosses Gewächs must be.

records.table: Pear, kumquat and a salty finish mark Horst Sauer's dry Escherndorfer Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG, from the steep, south facing heart of the Lump, on shell limestone above a bend of the Main. Its own wild yeasts and long months on the lees shape it.
records.story: Above Escherndorf, beside a tight loop of the Main, the Lump climbs in a steep, south facing amphitheatre of shell limestone. Its heart takes its name from a document: by the VDP's account the field name Am Lumpen first appears in a description of goods and statutes in 1655, and the year became part of the name of the Grosse Lage. As the house tells it, the Sauer family had tended vines on the Lump for many generations, but the estate that carries the founder's name is young. In 1971 the founder and his father planted the Hütte parcel on the Lump, the first vineyard the founder set himself, and the estate grew from a small start on the Lump and the neighbouring Fürstenberg. It joined the VDP in 2001. The library knows it as the Franken estate a candidate should name for serious dry Silvaner, and for botrytis wines of rare clarity from the same slope. Another Escherndorf house, Rainer Sauer, bottles a wine from the same site under the same name, so the first name on the label matters. What shell limestone and a steep southern slope make of Franken's own grape is the lesson this bottle sets.

traps: Weingut Rainer Sauer is a separate Escherndorf estate that also bottles an Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG; read the first name.
Am Lumpen 1655 is the Grosse Lage at the heart of the Escherndorfer Lump, not a different village or a Grosslage.
The Lump is shell limestone, Muschelkalk, not the red sandstone of the Mainviereck or the gypsum Keuper of the Steigerwald.

With a cultured yeast in new barriques
On its skins for weeks, like a red wine
With added sugar to leave it sweet

The founder and his daughter are living and are not named; the father who planted the Hütte with him in 1971 is not named either, his dates unknown.
Founded is empty: the house says it was founded by the founder on a small holding but gives no year, and 1971 is the planting of a parcel.

Left out for want of a source: the year of the first bottling under the house's own name, the vessel (steel or cask) for the GG, and any claim that the house was first to make dry Lump Silvaner of this rank.
The serving and ageing lines follow the Codex's service reference and the trade's general reading; no vintage figure is used.

The VDP calls the record of 1655 a description of goods and regulations; Rainer Sauer's account calls it a wine tax document. The record follows the VDP.

wine.name: Würzburger Stein Silvaner GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Stein-Berg, a VDP.Grosse Lage within the Würzburger Stein
wine.sites: The Stein-Berg, the curved heart of the Würzburger Stein above the city and a VDP Grosse Lage: steep, at 30 to 75 per cent and some 190 to 280 metres, on middle shell limestone, its greater part shared by the Juliusspital, the Bürgerspital and the Staatlicher Hofkeller.
wine.making: By the foundation's own account its leading wines mature in the large oak casks of its historic cask cellar beneath the hospital, some two hundred and twenty of them, beside a smaller stock of barriques and tonneaux; the Grosses Gewächs is bottled dry.
wine.glass: Yellow pear, forest honey and dried fig over smoke and crushed stone, with the grip of shell limestone; dry, full and tactile, with a long, savoury finish.
wine.ageing: Firm when young, it opens after three or four years and gains honey and smoke over a decade and more in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour or let it open in the glass; a white wine glass.

label.means: The city and the Grosse Lage within the Stein, the name the GG carries from about the 2019 vintage.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.
The wine estate of the charitable foundation of 1576, which pays for its hospital and care homes.

records.table: A Würzburg charity of 1576 whose vineyards were given to pay for its hospital, the Juliusspital takes its Würzburger Stein Silvaner GG from steep shell limestone above the city. Matured in large oak casks, it is dry and full: pear, honey and smoke.
records.story: On 12 March 1576 Julius Echter von Mespelbrunn (1545 to 1617), Prince Bishop of Würzburg from 1573, laid the foundation stone of a great hospital with an almshouse and an orphanage, and in 1579 he endowed it. He gave it farms, forests and vineyards so that it could pay its own way, and that design has held: by the foundation's own account the proceeds of its agriculture, its forests and its wine estate finance its hospital and its care for the old and the sick. A stone relief of the foundation shows the gifts, and by Wines of Germany's account it carries a flask that some read as an early picture of a Bocksbeutel, though it may have held medicine. The historic cask cellar beneath the hospital, as the house tells it, holds some two hundred and twenty large oak casks for the wines of its leading sites. The chief of those is the Würzburger Stein, the shell limestone hill above the city whose wine was long called Steinwein, its greater part shared among the Juliusspital, the Bürgerspital and the Staatlicher Hofkeller. Silvaner is the house's main grape, and its Grosses Gewächs from the Stein, labelled Stein-Berg from about the 2019 vintage, is its reading of the city's own hill. In the glass it is Würzburg Silvaner as a charity has made it for four and a half centuries.

others.name: Iphöfer Julius-Echter-Berg Silvaner GG
others.note: A Silvaner Grosses Gewächs from Iphofen in the Steigerwald, the site named for the founder.

others.name: Würzburg Stein Silvaner Erste Lage
others.note: The dry Silvaner from the wider Stein, ranked a step below the Grosses Gewächs.

others.name: Würzburg Stein-Berg Riesling GG
others.note: Riesling from the same Grosse Lage, beside the Silvaner.

traps: The Juliusspital was founded by a Prince Bishop in 1576; the Bürgerspital by a patrician couple in 1316. Do not swap the dates.
From about the 2019 vintage the Stein GG reads Würzburg Stein-Berg; it is the same hill, not a new village or a different estate.
The Julius-Echter-Berg is at Iphofen, on gypsum Keuper in the Steigerwald, not in Würzburg.

cards.front: Who founded the Juliusspital in Würzburg, and in what year?

cards.front: Juliusspital's Silvaner GG: on what soil does its Würzburg site grow?

A village east of Würzburg
A sweet Prädikat level
The foundation's second label
questions.exp: The VDP lists the Stein-Berg as a Grosse Lage of the Stein above Würzburg; it is a vineyard, not a village or a sweetness level.

opts: So that it could pay for its hospital
To supply wine to the Bishop's court
To settle a debt to the city
To train monks in winegrowing
questions.exp: The endowment was meant to keep the hospital, almshouse and orphanage, and the estate's proceeds finance the foundation's care; it was not a court supply.

report: The plan names the wine Würzburger Stein Silvaner GG; Falstaff and wein.plus print Würzburg Stein-Berg Silvaner GG from about the 2019 vintage (the refuter found Falstaff listing a 2019 Stein-Berg GG and a 2015 Stein GG), and the VDP lists the Stein-Berg as the Grosse Lage. The name keeps the plan's words; the label term and a trap explain the newer form. No source said when or why the name changed.

The Stein rather than the Julius-Echter-Berg as the lead Silvaner is the plan's choice; the house makes GGs from both and no source ranks one over the other, so a swap to the Iphöfer Julius-Echter-Berg could be argued and is not proposed.
Julius Echter's dates are the Deutsche Biographie's, 18 March 1545 to 9 September 1617; the foundation stone of 12 March 1576 and the endowment of 1579 are the foundation's own history.
The cellar dating from 1576 and the 220 casks are the house's own account, with the importer for the cellar; a cask coopered from the foundation's own oak is the house's news page.

Left out for want of a source: hand picking, the fermenting yeast, the length of the cask ageing for the GG, the region record's claim of Lump holdings, and any size of the estate (volatile in any case).

changed: wine.sites: was 'facing south to south east at 210 to 285 metres, mostly terraced and steep, on weathered shell limestone with clay loam that throws light back onto the vines'; now the VDP's figures, 30 to 75 per cent and 190 to 280 metres on middle shell limestone, with the Stein-Berg's three chief owners; the aspect and the light were not found and are cut.

wine.making: 'some of them coopered from oak of the foundation's own forests and fitted with cooling plates' is cut, not found; now the house's own count of some 220 oak casks in the historic cask cellar, with barriques and tonneaux beside them.

story: 'A stone charter carved in 1576 shows the gifts, and Wines of Germany notes a Bocksbeutel among them' is now the relief of the foundation with a flask some read as an early Bocksbeutel, perhaps a medicine flask, as Wines of Germany and Wikipedia give it; 'the cellar under the hospital dates from the foundation' is cut, not found.
wine.label, story and traps: the Stein-Berg name is dated from about the 2019 vintage, was 2020: Falstaff lists a 2019 Würzburg Stein-Berg Silvaner GG and a 2015 Würzburg Stein Silvaner GG.
table and cards: 'terraces' and 'clay loam' are gone with the site line; now steep shell limestone.
open: The foundation stone is 12 March 1576 in the foundation's history and a museum document, 12 May 1576 in Wines of Germany; the record gives the year only in prose but the day is the foundation's.
The aspect of the Stein-Berg was not read in any source.

wine.name: Würzburger Stein-Harfe Silvaner GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Stein-Harfe, a VDP.Grosse Lage in sole ownership
wine.sites: The Stein-Harfe, stone harp in English, in the heart of the Würzburger Stein and held by the Bürgerspital alone: a steep slope of shell limestone planted with old vines.
wine.making: By the house's own sheets the grapes stay long on their skins before pressing, the must ferments with its own yeasts in wooden casks, the Stück among them, the large traditional oak cask of German cellars, and the wine then rests on its fine lees in wood before it is bottled dry.
wine.glass: Quince, yellow apple and dried herbs over wet stone and a smoky, salty note; dense and concentrated for Silvaner, dry, with a fine bitter edge and a long finish.
wine.ageing: Closed for its first years, it opens after four or five and keeps well over a decade, gaining honey, smoke and herbs.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour, or pour it slowly; a white wine glass.

label.means: The city and the Grosse Lage in the Stein that the Bürgerspital owns alone.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.
Dry by the legal measure, as every Grosses Gewächs must be.

records.table: The Bürgerspital, Würzburg's older charity, founded in 1316, alone owns the corner of the Stein that gives its Würzburger Stein-Harfe Silvaner GG. Its own yeasts ferment it in wooden casks, the Stück among them, and the wine is dense, smoky and salty.
records.story: In 1316 a wealthy Würzburg patrician and his wife gave their property to the city to house the sick and the needy, and the Bürgerspital zum Heiligen Geist grew from that gift, enlarged by later endowments of the city's citizens; its wine estate helps to pay for its care. Its treasure was its share of the Würzburger Stein. By the account of Wines of Germany, Silvaner was first planted in the Stein in 1665, by a Cistercian abbot. In 1726 the city council moved against the adulteration of wine: the Bürgerspital's Steinwein of the 1718 vintage was filled in its cellars into Bocksbeutel flasks of about a litre and sealed with the city's seal, and the squat flask became Franken's emblem. The Stein-Harfe is a VDP Grosse Lage held by the Bürgerspital alone, so its dry Silvaner is the one wine of the Stein that only one house can make. For a sommelier it teaches the Stein and the Bocksbeutel in one bottle.

others.name: Würzburger Stein Silvaner 1G Erste Lage
others.note: The dry Silvaner from the house's wider holding in the Stein, ranked a step below the Grosses Gewächs.

others.name: Würzburger Stein-Harfe Riesling Spätlese
others.note: A sweet Riesling from the same monopole, a Prädikat wine beside the dry Grosses Gewächs.

traps: The Bürgerspital, founded in 1316 by citizens, is older than the Juliusspital, founded by a Prince Bishop in 1576.
The Würzburger Stein is shared by several houses; the Stein-Harfe within it is the Bürgerspital's alone.
The Bocksbeutel decree of 1726 sealed Steinwein of the 1718 vintage; the flask is the region's, not one house's bottle.

cards.back: Riesling, as a Spätlese and in some years an Auslese.

It is a brand for wine bought in

questions.q: In which year was the Bürgerspital zum Heiligen Geist founded in Würzburg?
questions.exp: A patrician couple endowed it in 1316; 1576 is the Juliusspital's founding, 1665 Silvaner's first planting in the Stein and 1726 the Bocksbeutel decree.

Bürgerspital Weingut: 2024 Würzburger Stein-Harfe Silvaner GG trocken

report: The founders are described, not named: Wikipedia and Wines of Germany name Johannes von Steren and his wife Mergardis, but Steren's dates (about 1270 to 1329) are in one source only.

The 1726 decree and the 1718 vintage rest on Wines of Germany, the house's own account through Tageskarte and the city of Würzburg's portal; Wines of Germany says one litre, Tageskarte one Mass of about 1.22 litres, so the record says about a litre.
Silvaner in the Stein in 1665 by a Cistercian abbot is Wines of Germany with the house's Stein page; the abbot's name is left out for want of his dates.
Left out: Wines of Germany's note that the cellar holds a Steinwein of 1540, since the famous 1540 Steinwein is elsewhere tied to the royal cellar and the claim needs a second source.
The Stück is not given a size: no source read stated the capacity of the house's casks.

wine.making: now the house's sheet of the 2024 vintage: long skin contact, wild fermentation in wooden casks, the Stück among them, fine lees in wood; the 2016 sheet gives cool fermentation in steel, so the method is not timeless.

sources: Tageskarte and the 2018 sheet give way to the house's 2024 sheet and the city of Würzburg's page on the Bocksbeutel, which gives the sealing from the 1718 vintage.
open: The sealing of the 1718 vintage rests on Wines of Germany, the city's portal and the house's own account; no archival study was read.
The founders' dates (Johannes von Steren, about 1270 to 1329) are in Wikipedia alone; the founders stay described, not named.

records.place: Bürgstadt on the Main, in the Mainviereck, Franken

wine.name: Bürgstadter Hundsrück Spätburgunder GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Hundsrück, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Bürgstadt
wine.grapes: Spätburgunder, the German name for Pinot Noir, alone.
wine.sites: The Hundsrück at Bürgstadt, the eastern parcels of the Bürgstadter Berg: a steep slope of about 35 per cent facing south at 170 to 230 metres, on weathered Buntsandstein, red sandstone that is iron rich, stony and free draining.
wine.making: Fermented on its skins in open wooden vats, with a high share of whole bunches, at times all of them, by the house's pages, then basket pressed. It matures for between twelve and twenty months, by the house's pages, in Burgundian barrels of 228 litres, rests long on its lees, clears in the barrel and is bottled unfiltered.
wine.glass: Red cherry, redcurrant and wild strawberry over cloves, forest floor and a smoky, stony edge; firm, fine tannin, bright acidity and a long, spiced finish.
wine.ageing: Tight for its first five years, it opens slowly and keeps well beyond a decade in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 15 to 16 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Burgundy glass.

label.means: The village and the Grosse Lage, a name restored to its own site in 2010.
Pinot Noir, under its German name.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.

records.table: Red sandstone on a steep slope of the Main, in the west of Franken, gives Rudolf Fürst its Bürgstadter Hundsrück Spätburgunder GG. Open wooden vats and Burgundian barrels make a firm, spiced Pinot Noir, and a young bottle wants an hour in a decanter.
records.story: The Fürst family has been recorded as winegrowers in Bürgstadt, on the Main in the west of Franken, since 1638, by its own history. The Hundsrück above the village is older on paper: the VDP records that it was assessed for tax in 1564. The wine law of 1971 folded it into the larger Centgrafenberg, and the name left the labels for nearly four decades. In 1979 the family built a new estate house among the vines of the Centgrafenberg, and in the years that followed it turned to red wine raised in small Burgundian barrels, on the iron rich red sandstone of the hill. In 2010 the Hundsrück was entered again in Franken's official register of vineyards as a site of its own, and the house calls it its flagship site, the one that gives its most powerful and spicy Spätburgunder each year. By its own pages the house ferments its reds in open wooden vats, often with a high share of whole bunches. Where else in Germany does Pinot Noir grow on red sandstone? The exam asks, and this wine answers.

others.name: Klingenberger Schlossberg Spätburgunder GG

traps: The Hundsrück at Bürgstadt is a vineyard in Franken, not the Hunsrück hills between the Mosel and the Nahe.
Bürgstadt lies in the Mainviereck on red sandstone, not on the shell limestone of Würzburg and Escherndorf.
Spätburgunder is Pinot Noir; Frühburgunder is its early ripening mutation, a different wine of the same house.

cards.front: Rudolf Fürst's Hundsrück: on what rock does the vineyard grow?
cards.back: Weathered red to orange Buntsandstein, iron rich red sandstone, on a steep slope facing south.

cards.front: Fürst's Hundsrück Spätburgunder GG: when did the vineyard lose its own name, and when did it regain it?
cards.back: It was folded into the Centgrafenberg by the wine law of 1971 and entered again as its own site in the official register in 2010.

questions.q: A guest asks how Fürst's Hundsrück Spätburgunder GG is raised. Which description fits the house's pages?
opts: Open wooden vats, then Burgundian barrels
Stainless steel, then bottled young
Carbonic maceration in sealed tanks
Concrete eggs, then large old casks only
questions.exp: The house ferments its reds on the skins in open wooden vats and ages them twelve to twenty months in 228 litre Burgundian barrels; steel and early bottling are wrong.

questions.q: Since when has the Fürst family been recorded as winegrowers in Bürgstadt, by its own history?
questions.exp: The family dates its winegrowing in Bürgstadt to 1638; 1564 is the Hundsrück's tax record, 1971 the law that merged it and 1979 the new estate house.

report: The Hundsrück as the house's flagship rests on the house's own pages and two trade accounts; the plan's pick stands.
Founded is empty: the family's record from 1638 is a first record, and 1979 is the building of the estate house, not a founding.
The family members who run the estate are living and are not named; Rudolf Fürst, whose name the house carries, is not given dates, since none were found.
Barrel time is twelve to twenty months on the house's German cellar page and thirteen to eighteen on its English page, so the record says between twelve and twenty, hedged as the house's pages.
Sources disagree on whether the Hundsrück lies within the Centgrafenberg or beside it; the record follows the VDP: merged in 1971, its own site again from 2010.
Left out for want of a second source: the first vintage bottled under the Hundsrück name, any share of new oak, the share of whole bunches for this wine, and the Klingenberger Schlossberg's soil.

changed: story: 'Since 2010 the VDP has listed the Hundsrück again' is wrong in kind: it was entered again in Franken's official register of vineyards in 2010 (the VDP's own page and the house's); now so, with card 2.

story: 'one of the German pioneers of red wine raised in small Burgundian barrels' and 'made the Mainviereck known as red wine country' are cut as claims of rank with no second source; 'By 2016, as a trade profile ... more whole bunches' is now the house's own pages: open wooden vats, often a high share of whole bunches.
wine.sites: adds the VDP's slope of about 35 per cent and the eastern parcels of the Bürgstadter Berg; 'red to orange' is cut.
wine.making: the share of whole bunches is now the house's 'high share, at times all of them'.
open: The house also cites a document of 1525 naming the Hundsrück; the record keeps the VDP's tax record of 1564.
The new estate house of 1979 is in wein.plus and Wines of Germany; another trade source puts a handover in 1979.

wine.name: Casteller Schlossberg Silvaner GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Schlossberg, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Castell in sole ownership
wine.sites: The Schlossberg, the old castle hill above Castell on the western edge of the Steigerwald: a steep slope of 40 to 70 per cent facing west at some 340 to 370 metres, on Keuper with gypsum, alabaster and shale, held by the estate alone.
wine.making: By the house's own sheets the grapes are given a short contact on their skins before pressing, the must ferments spontaneously with its own yeasts, and the wine matures in casks of Casteller wood, oak from the estate's own forests, before it is bottled dry.
wine.glass: Green pear, hay and white pepper over chalk dust and a salty note; dry, robust and spiced, with texture from the cask and a long, firm finish.
wine.ageing: Firm in youth, it opens after three to five years; the house's sheets give it up to twenty years, and in some vintages thirty.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour or let it open in the glass; a white wine glass.

label.means: The village and the Grosse Lage below the castle, owned by the estate alone.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.
Franken's grape, called Österreicher at Castell when it was first planted there.

records.table: The Castell estate in the Steigerwald dates its first Silvaner to the foot of its own Schlossberg in 1659, and its Casteller Schlossberg Silvaner GG grows on that slope, on gypsum Keuper. Its own yeasts, then casks of the estate's own oak, give a robust, peppery and salty Silvaner.
records.story: The family of Castell traces its line to a presumed ancestor recorded in 1057, and its village lies on the western edge of the Steigerwald, where the vines grow on gypsum Keuper. The house dates its own winegrowing to 1224, when the counts deeded property to the monastery of Ebrach, and the VDP tells of a division of the counts' lands about 1266 whose charter first named Castell's chief vineyards, the Schlossberg and the Hohnart among them. Then came the entry the house keeps as its charter. On 6 April 1659, by the account of the house and of Wines of Germany, twenty five Austrian cuttings were set at the foot of the Schlossberg: Silvaner, long called Österreicher. A purchase record in the princely archive holds the entry, and by its own account the house is the home of German Silvaner, its first recorded planting. The Schlossberg is held by the estate alone and ranked a VDP Grosse Lage, planted to Silvaner. Its Grosses Gewächs carries the whole story: the grape, the slope where the house says it was first set in Germany, and the family that set it. Ask where Silvaner's German life began, and the house points to this slope.

traps: The Fürstlich Castell'sches Domänenamt of the Steigerwald has nothing to do with Rudolf Fürst of Bürgstadt; Fürstlich means princely.
Castell grows on gypsum Keuper in the Steigerwald, not on the shell limestone of Würzburg and Escherndorf.
Castell dates German Silvaner to 1659; the Würzburger Stein's first Silvaner is dated 1665. Keep the two apart.

cards.front: Castell's Schlossberg Silvaner GG: what was planted at the foot of the Schlossberg on 6 April 1659?
cards.back: Twenty five Austrian cuttings, Silvaner, which the house holds to be the grape's first recorded planting in Germany.

cards.front: On what soil does the Casteller Schlossberg grow?
cards.back: Keuper clay with gypsum, alabaster and shale, on the western edge of the Steigerwald.

questions.exp: The house matures the GG in casks of Casteller wood, oak from its own forests; acacia and chestnut are other cask woods, not Castell's.

questions.q: By the house's account, in which year was the first Silvaner planted at Castell?
questions.exp: The cuttings were set on 6 April 1659; 1224 is the house's first record of winegrowing, 1266 the division naming its sites and 1665 the Stein's first Silvaner.

sources.title: Castell: Schlossberg Silvaner GG, VDP.Grosse Lage

report: The planting of 6 April 1659 is the house's claim, borne out by Wines of Germany and the importer; both describe twenty five Austrian cuttings at the foot of the Schlossberg, recorded in the princely archive. Told hedged as the house's account.

The official who recorded the 1659 planting and the count of the day are not named: a Franconian source names Johann Georg Körner, another names a Count Wolfgang Georg, and no dates were found for either.
Winegrowing from 1224 is the house's own date, with Wikipedia's deed to Ebrach; another house page says 1266, the VDP's division of the counts' lands. Both are told as what each source says.
Founded is empty: neither 1057 (an ancestor's first record), 1224 nor 1266 is a founding of the estate.
The house now styles itself Castell or Fürst Castell on its pages; the plan's name is kept.
Left out for want of a source: the date the counts became princes, hand picking, and the length of cask ageing for the GG; the princely family is told with no living name.

changed: wine.sites: adds the VDP's slope of 40 to 70 per cent, the westward aspect (the house's sheet and the VDP's German page; the English page says south and west) and some 340 to 370 metres.
wine.ageing: 'the house gives it a span of ten to thirty years' is now up to twenty, thirty in some vintages: the 2018 sheet says ten to thirty, the 2020 sheet up to twenty.
story: the ancestor of 1057 is now a presumed ancestor, as the Göttingen Academy's lexicon has it; the division of about 1266 now names the Schlossberg and the Hohnart, as the VDP's page reads.

others: the Hohnart's 'aged a year on its lees in Castell oak' and the Kugelspiel's 'partly in casks, partly in steel' are cut as unsourced; the Kugelspiel is now named an Erste Lage as the house's sheet titles it.
open: The planting of 6 April 1659 is the house's archive, borne out by Wines of Germany and the importer; Wikipedia gives 5 April. Told as the house's account.
The house says it holds its GGs five years in the castle cellar before release; not added, as one sheet only.
